title: Cities: Skylines | Franklin, Episode 8: TRAINS!
premise: Donoteat uses Franklin's new railroads to argue that transformative speed coexisted with unsafe operations, land speculation, charter loopholes, fragmented private networks and dangerous labor; the historical claims are the presenter's.
coverage: Franklin's railroads introduce steam engines, wheel classification, unsafe travel, charter loopholes, incompatible gauges, and dangerous construction labor. Historical claims are the presenter's account; fictional railway spellings remain uncertain.

panels.heading: Primal craving
panels.description: A single DNE token sits in a black field while the narrator builds suspense.
panels.camera: Static central logo.
panels.visualGag: Spoken addiction setup; the visual payoff is the next panel.

panels.heading: TRAINS reveal
panels.description: Huge TRAINS lettering appears over a monochrome photograph of two locomotives.
panels.camera: Hard cut from logo to static card.
panels.visualGag: The dramatic craving monologue resolves into this oversized rail-enthusiast punchline.
panels.notes: The huge TRAINS card follows the spoken craving monologue.

panels.heading: Franklin titles
panels.description: Orange Franklin and Liberty Bell branding overlays the city; white A DONOTEAT SERIES appears beneath.
panels.camera: Changing aerial views, then black and a cut to gameplay.
panels.visualGag: The late-series joke is spoken rather than shown.

sound.text: Title music: Beethoven Symphony No. 5, IV. Allegro, as credited for the title sequence.

panels.heading: Waterfront to railroad
panels.description: Parallel sidings and platforms sit near streets and undeveloped gridded land.
panels.camera: Overhead gameplay changes framing and distance across the railway site.
panels.action: Track/platform selections and placement previews change.
panels.notes: The presenter connects the waterfront to episode 6's Good Hill Water Works.

panels.heading: Two lines, not three
panels.description: A fan of sidings spreads from the railway junction.
panels.camera: Closer overhead framing than earlier town-wide shots.
panels.action: The player selects track and rolling-stock props around the junction.

panels.heading: Steam origins introduction
panels.description: The railway-build gameplay continues; STEAM ENGINES appears over the sidings before the ancient-machine engraving is inserted.
panels.camera: Overhead gameplay reframes the sidings and buildings beneath the section title.
panels.action: Rolling-stock props and selections change in the rail yard.

panels.heading: Ancient steam novelty
panels.description: An aeolipile engraving is overlaid on the build footage.
panels.camera: Static engraving over changing gameplay.

panels.heading: Newcomen mine pump
panels.description: A cutaway engraving shows a beam pump, cylinder and boiler structure.
panels.camera: Static pump illustration over gameplay, then a cut back to the build.
panels.notes: The historical account is the presenter's.

panels.heading: Trevithick locomotive
panels.description: A monochrome drawing shows a high-pressure locomotive with a large flywheel.
panels.camera: Static locomotive illustration, then gameplay.

panels.heading: Steam lesson begins
panels.description: A deliberately rough brown locomotive sits under a turquoise sky and a smiling sun in sunglasses; a cutaway exposes the firebox.
panels.camera: Static side-on diagram gains graphic details.
panels.visualGag: The smiling sunglasses sun adds a cheerful, childish touch to the steam lesson.

panels.heading: Inside a boiler
panels.description: A rust-colored cutaway boiler photograph exposes the tubes.
panels.camera: Hard cut to static photograph, then back to diagram.

panels.heading: Pressure building
panels.description: BOILER and FIREBOX arrows point to a cutaway drawn locomotive with horizontal tubes.
panels.camera: Static side-on diagram.
panels.visualGag: The smiling sunglasses sun remains through the boiler lesson.

panels.heading: Piston stroke
panels.description: A cylinder close-up shows a labeled PISTON, pipes and hand-drawn arrows.
panels.camera: Cut from whole-engine view to fixed diagram close-up.
panels.action: The piston changes position as arrows reverse direction.
panels.visualGag: Smiling sunglass sun persists through the piston lesson, continuing the earlier playful drawing motif.
panels.notes: The exact intermediate piston motion is unclear.

panels.heading: Valve gear photograph
panels.description: A monochrome close-up of real driving wheels and connecting gear interrupts the diagram.
panels.camera: Hard cut to static photograph, then return.
panels.action: Static photo; no operating motion shown.

panels.heading: Alternating pressure
panels.description: The same cylinder returns with changed piston position and opposing arrows.
panels.camera: Fixed diagram framing, changing graphic states.
panels.action: The piston moves between alternate positions.
panels.visualGag: Smiling sunglass sun remains during changing piston/steam-arrow states, continuing the earlier drawing motif.

panels.heading: Wheels and rods
panels.description: Whole-engine drawing labels SIDE RODS and then TRAILING WHEELS; the sunglass sun remains.
panels.camera: Cut back to the whole-engine diagram as labels change.
panels.visualGag: The smiling sunglasses sun remains through the wheel-and-rod lesson.
panels.notes: The rough diagram is not a scale engineering drawing.

panels.heading: Classification prelude
panels.description: Overhead gameplay shows track sidings beside industrial buildings before the wheel-classification title appears.
panels.camera: Cut from the diagram back to changing overhead views of the railway.
panels.action: The railway selection and placement interface stays visible.

sound.text: Whyte-classification music: Brahms's Tragic Overture, as credited for this sequence.

panels.visualGag: The coming THE WHYTE SYSTEM title sets up a white/Whyte homophone joke with a disclaimer about racism.

panels.heading: Whyte system / white-system setup
panels.description: Large white THE WHYTE SYSTEM lettering overlays the overhead siding build, still without its disclaimer.
panels.camera: The title overlays overhead gameplay as the siding view widens.
panels.action: Track-selection circles and gameplay interface remain visible while the title stays centered.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the disclaimer payoff: Whyte sounds like white, inviting a racial reading before NOT A RACIST THING, JUST THE GUY'S NAME appears.

panels.heading: Whyte disclaimer payoff
panels.description: THE WHYTE SYSTEM now has a second line: (NOT A RACIST THING, JUST THE GUY'S NAME), over the same railway-build gameplay.
panels.camera: Centered title and new subtitle over a wider overhead siding view.
panels.action: A subtitle appears beneath the title while the track-selection interface remains visible.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the preceding Whyte/white homophone setup: an unsolicited anti-racist disclaimer clarifies that the name refers to a person. The next Thomas panel returns to the straight classification lesson.

panels.heading: Thomas as engineering specimen
panels.description: Thomas the Tank Engine from Thomas & Friends, blue with his smiling face and three pairs of driving wheels appears over gameplay.
panels.camera: Static character photograph over changing overhead build views.
panels.action: No character movement in the insert.
panels.visualGag: After the Whyte/white disclaimer, Thomas becomes an engineering specimen and sets up Henry's tunnel interruption.

panels.heading: Henry setup
panels.description: Henry, the green engine from Thomas & Friends, appears with 4-6-0 classification text.
panels.camera: Static insert over gameplay; text added.
panels.visualGag: Worried Henry is the setup for the literal tunnel imprisonment in the next panel.

panels.heading: Henry payoff
panels.description: Henry from Thomas & Friends peers out above a brick wall built across a tunnel mouth.
panels.camera: Hard cut to the static tunnel photograph.
panels.action: Henry is visibly blocked; no live bricklaying action.
panels.visualGag: The engineering lesson is derailed by the character's imprisonment: wheel arrangement becomes irrelevant.

sound.text: Sad trombone (wah-wah) punctuates “Although he's stuck in a tunnel, so it doesn't matter.” Henry from Thomas & Friends is bricked into the tunnel, making his wheel classification comically beside the point.

panels.heading: Gordon / Pacific
panels.description: Gordon, the smiling blue engine from Thomas & Friends, and his tender illustrate 4-6-2, with classification text added below.
panels.camera: Brief return to gameplay, then static photo insert.
panels.visualGag: Gordon returns the lesson to wheel classification after Henry's tunnel punchline.

panels.heading: Articulated A-class
panels.description: A large Norfolk and Western steam locomotive fills an inserted photograph.
panels.camera: Static insert over gameplay.
panels.action: No locomotive movement in the photograph.

panels.heading: East African class 59
panels.description: A long articulated locomotive with separate end wheel groups is shown in a color photograph.
panels.camera: Gameplay briefly reappears before a static insert.

panels.heading: Taxonomy breaks
panels.description: A monochrome side-view tank locomotive has an unusual wheel arrangement.
panels.camera: Hard cut from gameplay to a static photo.
panels.visualGag: The irregular visual example supplies the anti-climax to the orderly classification lecture.
panels.notes: The odd locomotive's identity is uncertain.

panels.heading: Speed versus pull
panels.description: A PRR locomotive photograph appears amid freight shed and rail-yard construction.
panels.camera: Static locomotive inserts alternate with overhead gameplay; K4s and L1s photos are separate cuts.
panels.action: Buildings and rail-car props are placed in the gameplay.
panels.notes: The presenter compares K4s and L1s locomotives; visible lettering does not identify every image.

panels.heading: Experimental designs introduction
panels.description: Gameplay shows the industrial rail yard and a selected warehouse roof while the narrator introduces experimental locomotive failures.
panels.camera: Overhead view of the selected warehouse before the Crampton photograph.

panels.heading: Crampton failure
panels.description: Monochrome locomotive photo shows a very large driving wheel toward its rear.
panels.camera: Static photo over gameplay.

panels.heading: Fontaine wheel scheme
panels.description: Locomotive engraving shows a huge upper wheel above lower wheels.
panels.camera: Static locomotive engraving.

panels.heading: Holman grift setup
panels.description: A monochrome locomotive photo shows small wheels stacked beneath the driving wheels.
panels.camera: Static photo, then a return to gameplay.
panels.visualGag: Visibly elaborate wheel-stacking prepares the modern transport-hype punchline.

panels.heading: Hyperloop punchline
panels.description: A green station/pod promotional render explicitly reads HYPERLOOP.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static render, then back to gameplay.
panels.action: Illustrated figures stand beside the futuristic pod; no visible movement.
panels.visualGag: Hyperloop appears as the visual answer to the Holman stock-swindle analogy.
panels.notes: The Hyperloop comparison is the presenter's satire, not a finding of fraud.

panels.heading: Fleet of John Bulls
panels.description: Museum photo shows an early small steam locomotive; gameplay builds long sheds and parallel yards.
panels.camera: Static insert then close and wide overhead gameplay reframing.
panels.notes: The fleet is described as 2-4-0 John Bulls; the fictional railway names remain uncertain.

panels.heading: Cars by cargo
panels.description: Freight- and passenger-car images alternate, including a modern red boxcar.
panels.camera: Static image inserts separated by gameplay cuts.

panels.heading: Terrifying speed setup
panels.description: Overhead rail-yard view shows converging tracks, platforms and sheds.
panels.camera: Changing overhead views of the rail yard.
panels.visualGag: The absurd uterus-speed rumor plays over an ordinary rail-yard build before NO, SERIOUSLY acknowledges how implausible it sounds. No flying anatomy appears.

panels.heading: No, seriously
panels.description: Large white (NO, SERIOUSLY) overlays the build footage.
panels.camera: Text overlay on overhead gameplay, gone shortly afterward.
panels.visualGag: Editorial insistence acknowledges how unbelievable the uterus-speed rumor sounds.

panels.heading: Comfort and manual braking
panels.description: A black-and-white photograph shows a railway worker crouching at a handbrake beside a rail vehicle.
panels.camera: Static insert, then gameplay returns.
panels.action: Worker is frozen in the photograph; no running animation is shown.

panels.heading: Street-running danger
panels.description: A bright red cowcatcher dominates a locomotive front photograph.
panels.camera: Static cowcatcher photograph amid street-and-track construction.
panels.action: Smoke-trailing trains move through gameplay; the photograph stays still.

panels.heading: Catastrophic collision
panels.description: A photograph shows one wooden rail car thrust into another.
panels.camera: Static insert, then a cut back to gameplay.
panels.notes: The photograph shows telescoped wooden cars; stove fires are discussed separately.

panels.heading: Charter powers
panels.description: RIGHT-OF-WAY text appears over gridded land, buildings and railway tracks.
panels.camera: Caption over overhead gameplay with changing angle and distance.

panels.heading: Uninhabited correction
panels.description: Photograph shows a teepee with Native people seated beside it.
panels.camera: Static overlay, then gameplay returns.
panels.visualGag: Visible residents puncture the narrator's sarcastic uninhabited premise.

panels.heading: Land profits and vague charters
panels.description: A red Pennsylvania Railroad keystone emblem overlays housing construction.
panels.camera: A brief static logo insert; otherwise top-down gameplay reframing.

panels.heading: Monopoly workaround
panels.description: Overhead gameplay shows parallel streets, railway tracks and long industrial buildings while the narrator introduces the Washington-access dispute.
panels.camera: Overhead gameplay reframes between housing blocks and the railway approaches.
panels.action: Building/rail selections change; no literal monopoly negotiation is enacted.
panels.visualGag: The Washington-access dispute leads through the B&O emblem to Bowie's place-name pun and the branch/main-line reversal.

panels.heading: Baltimore and Ohio monopoly holder
panels.description: A large navy-and-gold circular emblem bearing B&O and a Capitol dome overlays the railway-build footage.
panels.camera: Static emblem centered over overhead gameplay.
panels.action: The emblem is static; the underlying railway interface remains visible.
panels.notes: B&O identifies the railroad whose Washington monopoly Maryland protects in the presenter's account.

panels.heading: Baltimore and Potomac charter geography
panels.description: A regional map labels BALTIMORE over the gameplay, establishing the starting point for the Port Tobacco main-line and Washington-branch explanation.
panels.camera: Static Baltimore map, then gameplay.
panels.visualGag: The Baltimore map establishes the charter geography before Bowie's portrait and the ironic BRANCH LINE / MAIN LINE labels.

panels.heading: Bowie visual pun
panels.description: David Bowie's lightning-bolt portrait abruptly fills the center.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static portrait, gone about a second later.
panels.visualGag: The place name Bowie triggers an insert of the musician who shares it.
panels.notes: Bowie, Maryland, gets a brief David Bowie portrait.

panels.heading: Branch becomes main
panels.description: Junction aerial labels the Washington route BRANCH LINE and the Port Tobacco route MAIN LINE, both in quotation marks.
panels.camera: Static aerial/map graphic, then a return to gameplay.
panels.visualGag: The labels visualize the reversal between charter terminology and actual route importance.

panels.heading: Gauge incompatibility
panels.description: Two drawn rails beneath a sunglass sun are separated by an arrow labeled GAUGE.
panels.camera: Static diagram insert; gameplay resumes.
panels.visualGag: Sunglass sun returns as a visual callback to the steam diagrams; the odd nice-even gauge measurement is a separate spoken joke.

panels.heading: Transfer chaos
panels.description: Historical cartoon packs travelers, porters and baggage together beside TO THE BIRMINGHAM TRAIN signage.
panels.camera: Static insert; the crowd is not animated.
panels.action: The illustrated people lug baggage but do not move.
panels.visualGag: The crowded satirical image visually amplifies the inconvenience of changing nearly identical cars.
panels.notes: The cartoon is headed THE BREAK OF GAUGE AT GLOUCESTER.

panels.heading: Navvies: wages and catch
panels.description: Gameplay places housing blocks and reshapes the rail-side district.
panels.camera: Changing overhead angles and distances around housing and railway construction.
panels.action: Building previews and placements change; there is no navvy reenactment.
panels.notes: Navvies are described in narration; these game houses do not depict historical worker camps.

panels.heading: Fast, dirty, dangerous
panels.description: A large station-like building fronts the tracks in the growing district.
panels.camera: Overhead gameplay shifts to closer oblique station view, then back.
panels.action: Build selections change; trains appear in the rail-yard views around it.

panels.heading: Unsustainable schedule
panels.description: The rail-city construction montage continues as streets and house rows fill out.
panels.camera: Wide aerial and closer overhead gameplay alternate.

panels.heading: Greenwood bonus
panels.description: A monochrome historical street photograph shows people, cars and smoke rising beyond buildings.
panels.camera: Static photo, then gameplay returns.

panels.heading: Rent drive setup
panels.description: Housing and rail-yard gameplay continues during the $1 Patreon and rent appeal.
panels.camera: Top-down build views change angle and scale.
panels.visualGag: Spoken mock-commercial sets up the graphic rent-control punchline.

panels.heading: Rent control punchline
panels.description: RENT CONTROL fills a black screen in enormous white capitals.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a static full-screen card, then back to gameplay.
panels.visualGag: Proposed shirt slogan becomes an emphatic standalone graphic.

panels.heading: Thanks and transition
panels.description: Gameplay finishes house rows beside the railway before the screen goes black.
panels.camera: Overhead gameplay, then black.

panels.heading: City payoff
panels.description: UI-free aerial view shows train sidings, brick warehouses, street tracks and dense row houses.
panels.camera: An aerial sweep crosses the district; its exact path is uncertain.
panels.action: Trains and smoke are visible among the completed buildings.

sound.text: Cinematic music: Mendelssohn's The Hebrides, as credited for the closing city tour.

panels.heading: Waterfront sweep
panels.description: Aerial view shows piers and sheds alongside rails; a smoke-emitting train changes position.
panels.camera: The high view shifts sideways and rotates around the waterfront.
panels.action: The train advances along waterfront street tracks.

panels.heading: Rail-level ride
panels.description: Low view looks forward along street-embedded rails between tree-lined brick residences.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a low forward view as buildings pass beside the rails.
panels.action: The viewpoint advances along the rails; no protagonist appears.

panels.heading: Yard orbit
panels.description: High oblique view shows converging tracks, sheds, station and orange rail cars.
panels.camera: Cut back to changing aerial angles and distances around the yard.
panels.notes: The exact orbit or pan is uncertain.

panels.heading: Riverside district
panels.description: UI-free aerial passes the waterfront warehouse blocks and housing.
panels.camera: Cut to a waterfront angle, then a sweep along the river.
panels.action: A locomotive smoke plume changes position near the street track.

panels.heading: Street-running ride
panels.description: Low rails curve between industrial walls, then continue beside residential streets.
panels.camera: Hard cut to a low forward track view as landmarks pass.
panels.action: View advances along rails; buildings and track alignment change in foreground.

panels.heading: Final waterfront reveal
panels.description: Warehouses and piers fill the foreground, with the larger city behind.
panels.camera: A brief high street view, then a cut to a river-facing view; an aerial sweep widens the perspective.
panels.action: A smoke-emitting train advances near the waterfront.

panels.heading: Patron credits
panels.description: White patron names scroll on black.
panels.camera: Names rise against a fixed black background.

panels.heading: Token returns
panels.description: The DNE token returns alone on black.
panels.camera: Static centered logo.
